intent.raw: Use two lanes: one for validating the MVP idea, and another to propose different angles for the problem. The objective is to understand whether this MVP is the most valid one.
intent.objective: Run a two-lane validation route for the current IDE Ergonomics MVP so the candidate MVP is tested against counterexamples and compared with genuinely different solution angles before implementation.
intent.operator_sentence: Use two lanes to validate if the IDE ergonomics MVP is the most valid one.

route_menu.context_hint: The current MVP candidate is three IDE action cards: candidate definition, handoff composer, and subagent fanout preview. The dispatch must decide whether that is the strongest first proof or whether another angle should win.

items.label: Three Card MVP
items.description: Validate candidate definition, handoff composer, and subagent fanout preview as the smallest useful proof.

items.label: Definition Only MVP
items.description: Start with only candidate definition capture and prove knowledge-substrate value before any handoff or subagent UX.

items.label: Handoff First MVP
items.description: Make handoff generation the first proof because it creates immediate continuity across sessions and agents.

items.label: Route Menu MVP
items.description: Start by exposing bounded sigil/spell route choices before building richer action cards.

technique_overlays.trigger: The operator needs to know if the three-card MVP is the most valid first proof rather than the first attractive idea.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Lane Z must test the MVP with counterexamples; Lane A must keep the underlying problem fixed and propose non-renamed alternatives. Parent synthesis chooses the non-dominated MVP candidate.

technique_overlays.trigger: The MVP can be tested with a small conversation scenario before any IDE implementation.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Lane Z uses at least one realistic conversation toy scenario and records failure interpretation.

technique_overlays.trigger: Multiple first-proof shapes are plausible and should be compared explicitly.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The final synthesis must select, reject, or defer each route menu item.

technique_overlays.trigger: IDE action cards can accidentally imply execution or promotion authority.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Every proposed MVP must name its owner, proof evidence, mutation boundary, and receipt or handoff requirement.

subagent_strategy.trigger: Two-lane validation requires separated ownership: one lane should stress-test the current MVP and the other should propose different angles without anchoring on it.
subagent_strategy.explanation: Role-bound sibling lanes reduce anchoring and create a clear parent synthesis point before implementation.
context: Current MVP candidate: candidate definition action, handoff composer popup, subagent fanout preview.
Underlying problem: Arcanum has strong workflow contracts, but users must manually notice when a conversation should become a definition, handoff, route, side node, or delegated run.
Decision need: choose the smallest first proof that best validates the value of IDE-side Arcanum ergonomics.

roles.purpose: Validate the current three-card MVP by building it out, testing it with at least one realistic counterexample, and naming the conditions where it fails.
roles.owns: MVP validation, counterexample, failure interpretation, and repaired version of the current MVP.

roles.purpose: Hold the same underlying problem fixed and propose genuinely different first-proof angles, not variants of the same three-card MVP.
roles.owns: Alternative MVP candidates, rejected variants, trade-off comparison, and strongest challenge to the current MVP.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Approve running the two-lane MVP validation with Lane Z for current-MVP validation and Lane A for alternative angles?

agents.residue: host-specific feasibility remains unverified; no runtime IDE or browser evidence was gathered
agents.reroute: repair current MVP into a bounded conversation-transition card or replace subagent preview with route menu in the first proof

agents.residue: host-specific IDE affordances remain unverified; no toy UI proof was run
agents.reroute: replace current MVP with bounded route-menu over conversation span and defer subagent fanout preview

steps.name: Frame underlying problem and MVP candidates
stop_conditions: block if the underlying problem is phrased as the current MVP solution
block if fewer than two viable MVP candidates are named

steps.name: Run Lane Z and Lane A in tension
convergence_criteria: Lane Z records at least one real counterexample against the current three-card MVP.
Lane A proposes at least two alternatives that are not renamed versions of the current MVP.
Both lanes score candidates against the same problem statement and criteria.
Parent synthesis can name a winner, a narrowed MVP, or a block with residue.
stop_conditions: block if Lane A only tweaks the current MVP
block if Lane Z has no counterexample
block if delegated agents are spawned without explicit user approval

steps.name: Adjudicate MVP validity
convergence_criteria: Candidate solves the underlying problem with the least implementation surface.
Candidate produces observable value without canonical Arcanum mutation.
Candidate has a clear owner and validation evidence.
Candidate can fail cheaply before host integration work begins.
stop_conditions: route to decision-gate if the trade-off is consequential and cannot be inferred

steps.name: Prepare next-route handoff
stop_conditions: handoff must name next owner: spellcraft, invoke, task-session, discipline-governance, or deferred

gates.condition: The underlying problem is independent of the current three-card MVP.
Lane Z validates the current MVP with counterexamples and Lane A proposes genuinely different angles.
Delegated two-lane execution requires explicit user approval before subagents are spawned.
MVP validation evidence cannot directly promote definitions, ontology, spells, sigils, or runtime surfaces.
The selected MVP is judged against value, implementation surface, proof cost, owner clarity, and boundary safety.

boundaries.contract: Two-lane subagent execution is only recommended by this dispatch and requires explicit user approval before runtime fanout.
Lane evidence can support a next route, but cannot directly promote reusable capabilities or canonical definitions.

authority.lifecycle: dispatch-spec validates route shape; refine or necronomicon may orchestrate after approval
authority.execution: future approved two-lane subagents or parent-led lane passes

state_namespaces.write_policy: route, lane receipts, synthesis, and handoff only
read-only unless a later owner route approves mutation
observability only when runtime execution occurs

promotion_splits.rule: Spell creation requires a later Spellcraft lifecycle route.
Knowledge promotion requires definitions-governance or ontology owner review.
Implementation requires an Invoke define/design or Task Session route with validation evidence.

promotion_guardrails: Two-lane validation is evidence for choosing an MVP, not proof that the MVP is implemented.
No canonical Arcanum or DomainSpec mutation from this dispatch.
No subagent execution without explicit user approval.
